response.text:
Between 22 and 24 September 2026, subject account C1066 sent seven outgoing wire transfers, all to Canadian counterparties, totalling 14,637.28 CAD. Each payment went to a different external account: EXT-2073, EXT-2248, EXT-2104, EXT-2012, EXT-2110, EXT-2214 and EXT-2023. The transactions were TX-00599 (2,229.80 on 2026-09-22), TX-00600 (2,128.04 on 2026-09-22), TX-00603 (2,477.79 on 2026-09-23), TX-00616 (1,772.67 on 2026-09-23), TX-00620 (1,217.71 on 2026-09-23), TX-00667 (2,758.46 on 2026-09-24) and TX-00668 (2,052.81 on 2026-09-24). Each amount was sent by wire over a short period, and the recipients appear to have no relationship to one another or to the account holder. Alert ALR-00004 was triggered by rule R6 on this activity.

These features match several FINTRAC indicators: the client sends wire transfers to multiple beneficiaries that do not correspond to the expected use of the account, the wires are frequent and large with no apparent relationship between sender and receivers, and the client is sending funds to multiple unrelated parties. Taken together, these facts give reasonable grounds to suspect that the funds may be linked to money laundering or terrorist financing, and that is why this report is being filed.

Not verified: the identities of the external recipients, the onward destination of the funds, and the customer's expected activity profile. No other open alerts were linked to C1066 or its direct counterparties.

Rules:
- Use only the facts given. Every transaction id, amount and date you mention must appear in the verified transactions, written exactly as given.
- Never mention anything listed under "Rejected claims": the verifier found it false or unsupported.
- Explain who, what, when, where, how and why: the subject account, the pattern of transactions, the counterparties, and the FINTRAC indicators that apply.
- State reasonable grounds to suspect. Do not conclude guilt or name an offence.
- Plain prose, 150 to 300 words, no headings, no lists, no markdown. Reply with the narrative only.
